about.title: Behind the lens
paragraphs: I have spent the last eight years learning that the best photograph is almost never the one people pose for. It is the half-second after — the laugh that breaks, the hand that reaches, the light that turns.

I work quietly and I work fast. Whether it is a three-day wedding, a studio portrait or a brand film with a full crew, my job is the same: make people forget the camera is there, then be ready when they do.

items.q: How far in advance should I book?
items.a: For weddings, six to twelve months is typical, and peak season dates go first. Portraits and commercial work can usually be arranged within two or three weeks. If your date is close, ask anyway — cancellations happen.

items.q: How many photographs will I receive?
items.a: A full wedding day is usually 400 to 600 edited frames. A portrait session is around 25 to 40. I deliver what is genuinely good rather than padding a number, and there is no extra charge per image.

items.q: When will I get the gallery?
items.a: A preview set of 20 to 30 images arrives within 48 hours. The complete gallery follows within two weeks, and films within four.
Yes, anywhere. Travel and accommodation are added at cost for anything beyond a two-hour drive, and I will always show you the numbers before you commit.
We shoot anyway. Overcast light is flattering and rain makes memorable pictures. I carry covers for the gear and will scout indoor options in advance.

items.q: Can we get both photo and video?
items.a: That is what I would recommend. Shooting stills and motion together means one team on the day, one consistent look across both, and a better price than hiring separately.
